name: O Circuit, round the Paine massif
why: Eight days all the way round the massif: the empty north side, John Gardner Pass over the Southern Ice Field, then the W back to the start.
book: Only counter-clockwise, and every camp must be booked in order before you enter (Las Torres, Vertice, CONAF). The back side opens around November and closes in early April.
water: Streams and camps; food at the huts on the W part only.
dangers: John Gardner Pass (1,200 m) is the most exposed point of the park: rangers open it only in the morning and close it in storms.
Deep mud and fallen trees on the descent to Paso camp.
turnaround: Leave Los Perros camp at first light: the pass must be crossed before the afternoon wind.

points.name: Hotel Las Torres, Torres del Paine
points.note: Day 1: north along the Paine river to Serón camp (13 km, 4 h). The loop is walked only counter-clockwise.

points.name: Refugio Dickson on Lago Dickson
points.note: Day 2: 18 km from Serón. The hut stands on a meadow, the Dickson glacier at the end of the lake.

points.name: Glaciar Los Perros
points.note: Day 3: 11.8 km up the forest to Los Perros camp; the glacier lake is 5 minutes above it.

points.name: John Gardner Pass, Southern Ice Field view
points.note: Day 4: 1,180 m, the top of the loop: Glaciar Grey and the Southern Ice Field fill the whole west. Then down to Paso camp.

points.name: Glaciar Grey hanging bridges
points.note: Day 5: the steep path along the glacier and over its hanging bridges to Refugio Grey.

points.name: Refugio Paine Grande on Lago Pehoé
points.note: Day 6: along Lago Grey to Paine Grande; then the W back east by Italiano and Los Cuernos to the start, 2-3 more days.
